Missed because the sweep searched "LERENA FELIGRESA" and her compound surname sits between those words.

source: Direccion de Cementerios, Montevideo - mortality return for December 1901
used_for: *** A THIRD INDEPENDENT RECORD OF LUIS EUGENIO'S DEATH, and it places his burial. *** "Relacion de los individuos que han fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901" lists LUIS LERENA LENGUAS against day 24, between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez. Agrees exactly with civil act No. 216 and with his widow's sworn statement of 1908. Found only by searching the COMPOUND surname - a search on LERENA does not reach a table of names.

source: Argentina, National Census 1895 - the household schedule of Gilberto Lerena, Seccion 21, Manzana 15
used_for: *** CITED SINCE WEEK ONE FOR NAMES; NEVER READ AS A HOUSEHOLD UNTIL NOW. *** Sixteen people on one page. It gives Gilberto a trade - CORREDOR DE COMERCIO; enters JUSTINIANA LENGUAS at 73 and VIUDA, so Don Luis Lerena was dead by 1895; resolves a contradiction this archive had flagged against itself (Maria E. C. is 26 and SOLTERA, not Gilberto's daughter); and finds *** JOSEFA "LERENA DE LERENA", a widow of 43 *** - almost certainly the Josefa Lerena who stood godmother at Montevideo in 1885.

source: Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo death registration No. 10 of 3 April 1947
used_for: *** THE LERENA TRAIBEL BRANCH PLACED AT LAST. *** JOSEFA LORENA LERENA TRAIBEL, died 2 April 1947 aged NINETY-SIX, born 1851, "Parents: AMBROCIA TRAIBEL, AVELINO LERENA". This archive has named that branch since its first week without ever placing Avelino. She is a strong candidate for the Josefa Lerena of the 1885 Montevideo font and the "Lerena de L. Josefa, 43, viuda" of Gilberto's 1895 Buenos Aires household - *** recorded as three separate rows and deliberately NOT merged, *** after this archive conflated two Arturo Lerenas in the same week.

source: Uruguay, Civil Registration - the Moratorio Lerena children, and the tree attachment behind them
used_for: *** THE RECORD THAT DEFLATED MY OWN CLAIM WITHIN THE HOUR. *** A JOSEFA LERENA appears as mother of Josefa, Eduardo and Maria MORATORIO LERENA, "Spouses: Fernando Moratorio" - index-level civil registration, real records. FamilySearch's TREE then attaches her to Josefa Lerena Traibel 1851-1947, which is SECONDARY. If that link holds, the 1895 census "Lerena de L." is the enumerator's shorthand for the household and NOT evidence of a Lerena-Lerena marriage.

source: ALEX - Historische Rechts- und Gesetzestexte, Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek (alex.onb.ac.at)
used_for: *** ASSESSED AND UNUSABLE TODAY, for a reason worth recording. *** Its full-text search returns "TOTAL (0)" plus "Diese Seite steht zur Zeit leider noch nicht zur Verfugung" for EVERY query - proved by controls: "Konsul", "Uruguay" and "Montevideo" each give the identical 166-byte response. A zero from a search that returns zero for everything is not evidence. The one genuine hook if it recovers is CONSULAR: Austria-Hungary had consulates at Montevideo and Buenos Aires and gazetted its consuls, and this family is exactly the class honorary consuls were drawn from.

source: Full-text search for the phrase "Sancho Lerena" - the Madrid notarial cluster
used_for: A real DON SANCHO LERENA appears in Madrid notarial records 1773-1808, among censos and chaplaincies. *** NOT OURS, on a date: ours was marrying at Canelones in January 1791 while this man transacts before a Madrid notary the same year. *** Recorded because it is exactly the find that gets mistaken for him later - right name, right decade, and a Spanish origin that would flatter this archive's own Andalusian hypothesis.

source: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion - two baptisms at Union, Montevideo, 8 March 1880
used_for: *** THE ACT THAT SETTLES JOSEFA, and converts a tree attachment into a parish record. *** Maria Carlota and Maria de las Mercedes Moratorio Lerena, "de Fernando Moratorio y Josefa Lerena", with maternal grandparents "AVELINO y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL". So Josefa Lerena Traibel married a MORATORIO - which kills this archive's own census reading of "Lerena de Lerena" on a document rather than on a tree. It also produces MERCEDES LERENA, godmother and very likely Josefa's sister.
